chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Suleyman ibn Amr al-Nakha'i who said, and Al-Husayn ibn Sayf narrated to me from his brother Ali, from Suleyman, from the one who mentioned it,

From Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the best of the servants, so he said: 'Those who, when they do good, are joyful, and when they commit sins, seek forgiveness, and when they are given, they are thankful, and when they are afflicted, they are patient, and when they are angry, they forgive.'
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the best servants according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Prophet’s description of the 'best servants' by highlighting a balanced spiritual temperament that combines joy in virtue with humility in error. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of gratitude (shukr), patience (sabr), and forgiveness (afw) as defining characteristics of the true believer (mu'min). The traits reflect a dynamic state of the heart that remains grounded in divine remembrance regardless of external circumstances.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Suleyman Bin Amro Al Nakhaie who said, ‘And Al Husayn Bin Sayf narrated to me from his brother Ali, from Suleyman, from the one who mentioned it,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> was asked about the best of the servants, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Those who, when they do good deed, are joyful, and when they commit sins, seek Forgiveness, and when they are Given (something), they are thankful, and when they are afflicted, they are patient, and when they are angry, they forgive’.
en.sarwar: 31. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Sulayman ibn ‘Amr al-Nakha’i who has said that narrated to him al-Husayn ibn Sayf from his brother Ali from Sulayman from those who he mentioned (in his book) from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Holy Prophet was asked about the best ones among the servants (of Allah). The Holy Prophet said, ‘They are those who enjoy doing good deeds, and ask forgiveness when they do bad deeds, thank when they are favored, exercise patience when they suffer and forgive when they are subjected to anger.’”
